name: Receipt voucher for an advance
definition: A receipt voucher is the document issued on receipt of an advance, under clause (d) of section 31(3). Rule 50 fixes eleven particulars, (a) to (k), including the amount of advance taken and the tax on it.
why_it_exists: An advance is money received before a supply. The receipt voucher records the tax on that money. Posting it as revenue would recognise a sale that has not happened.
inputs: whether the rate and nature of supply are determinable
outputs: the set of rule 50 particulars found
the set of mandatory particulars absent
preconditions: the document is issued under rule 50
exceptions: where the rate of tax is not determinable at receipt, tax is paid at eighteen per cent.
where the nature of supply is not determinable at receipt, the supply is treated as inter-State
rule 54(5) extends the rule 54(2) and 54(4) relaxations to receipt vouchers
common_mistakes: posting a receipt voucher as a sale — it evidences money received, not a supply made
treating the eighteen per cent. fallback as the rate of the eventual supply
expecting a quantity or a total invoice value — rule 50 requires the amount of advance taken, not either of those
legal_references: UNKNOWN — clause (d) of sub-section (3) of section 31 of the CGST Act was not read for this record
icai_references: UNKNOWN — the accounting treatment of an advance received is a separate question, not answered by the CGST Rules
gst_references: UNKNOWN — source is the Rules as at 01-01-2022; later amendments not held locally
evidence_required: the place of supply where inter-State
confidence_factors: weak when the document does not distinguish an advance from a payment against an invoice
weak when the eighteen per cent. fallback was applied, because the true rate was unknown even to the supplier
validation_checks: all eleven particulars (a) to (k) are present, subject to (i) applying only to inter-State supplies
the amount of advance taken is present
the voucher is not posted to a revenue account
examples: a voucher showing supplier GSTIN, serial number, date, customer details, description, advance amount, rate and amount of tax, reverse-charge flag and signature
counterexamples: a document showing an invoice total and a balance due — that is an invoice, not a receipt voucher

evidence.quote: 50. Receipt voucher.- A receipt voucher referred to in clause (d) of sub-section (3) of section 31 shall contain the following particulars, namely,-
the rate of tax is not determinable, the tax shall be paid at the rate of eighteen per cent.;
